newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: BUDGET BLUNDER WILL DESTROY CREDITIBILITY: EVANS
Shadow treasurer Gareth Evans says Australia's international economic credibility will suffer because of errors made in last year's Treasury forecasts.
The Treasury has admitted making 170 errors in buget forecasts, resulting in the general Government deficit being underestimated by more than one-billion dollars.
Mr Evans says making such a catstrophic blunder in the nation's accounts is extraordinarily embarrassing.
SEARCH FOR PRISONER SHOOTERS IN HUNTER VALLEY
Police in the Hunter Valley are searching for two men who allegedly tried to shoot a prisoner on day release at Rothbury near Cessnock.
A police spokeswoman says Corrective Services officers dropped the inmate off along Branxton Road and it's believed two men fired shots in the direction of the prisoner.
Police are at the scene and dog squads are searching the area.
COUNCIL SAYS GOVERNMENT GROSSLY NEGLIGENT
The state government's under pressure from a mid north coast council, which says it rushed to judgement over the possible source of water contamination at Wallis Lake.
The Great Lakes Council rejects the Environment Minister's accusations that it's been grossly negligent in not closing two sanitary depots near the lake as ordered by the E-P-A.
However, the council says it did close the depots, and yesterday gave the EPA a government report, showing groundwater has NOT been affected.
Meanwhile, the EPA's Brian Gilligan says the minister made her comments yesterday on the best available information.
COLSTON DEBATE HOTS-UP
Federal Industrial Releations Minister Peter Reith and Independent Senator Brian Harradine say the Labor Party is out to get former ALP, now Independent Senator, Mal Colston.
This follows an investigation into the Senator's parliamentary allowances and allegations he mis-used his position on the Australian National University board.
Peter Reith told ABC Radio that the A-L-P's been happy with the way the parliamentary allowances system worked for 13 years and is now rying to paint Senator Colston as the "Satan of the Senate".
Senator Harradine says the Labor Party's being foolish and working against its own best interests.
He told ABC radio the A-L-P's justified in wanting party members on certain committees, but says that's a separate issue to the financial allegations.
Meanwhile, Queensland Labor Senator Margaret Reynolds says Senator Colston should stand aside while the allegations are investigated.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
